findings.summary: docs/system-facts.md is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The guidance drops 'report the command and counts' and the post-fix soak report, so the 9daz gap (no recorded loop) is not closed
findings.evidence: The reading's guidance content says: '(1) reproduce it under parallel load on the base tree and report the command and counts ... (5) report a soak run after the fix'. The plan's own Decision 1 says 9daz's finding was 'no recorded 200-run loop'. The proposed paragraph says only 'counts failures before and after the fix' and never asks for the command or the counts to appear in the change description. The unit test pins no reporting phrase. A producer that runs the loop but does not report it would satisfy the text while repeating the 9daz failure, and the verifier would still have no evidence to judge. Fix: Add a short clause such as 'report the command and both failure counts in the change description' to the paragraph, and pin it in the_producer_brief_carries_the_flaky_test_guidance. To stay within budget, trim elsewhere: for example drop 'on threads' redundancy or shorten '(like stand_in_stress.rs; shell loops are denied)' to '(see stand_in_stress.rs; no shell loops)'. Re-estimate the size against the 1190 cap.
findings.location: Plan step 1 (paragraph text) and Decision 1; the reading's 'Guidance content' assumption items (1) and (5)

findings.summary: The prompt states two facts about this repository as if they were universal: the example file path and the shell-loop denial
findings.evidence: The capability prompt is compiled into Athena (lib.rs:21). Shell loops are denied only because athena.toml:84 lists no shell program for the producer, and that list is per-repository configuration ('read from the job's base commit', lib.rs:4-5). The bare file name 'stand_in_stress.rs' is not a path the producer can open directly. There is precedent for repo-specific references in this prompt (rendered-page-assertions.md, xtask site). Fix: Name the full path crates/athena-testkit/tests/stand_in_stress.rs if the byte budget allows, or write 'the Bash policy refuses shell loops' so the reason is attached to the policy and not stated as a fixed fact. The existing path assertion in the test already anchors the file.
findings.location: Plan step 1, '(like stand_in_stress.rs; shell loops are denied)'

findings.summary: The paragraph gives no route for a race that an in-process thread loop cannot reproduce
findings.evidence: The Risks section says 'The producer can say in its report why a loop cannot reproduce a given race', but the paragraph does not say so. The 2026-11 stand-in flake was a fork/exec race (ETXTBSY), and stand_in_stress.rs needed FORKERS to reproduce it. A pure thread loop would not have shown that race. Fix: Either add 'or say why a loop cannot show it' to the paragraph (budget permitting), or drop the mitigation claim from Risks so the plan does not rely on text it does not ship.

findings.summary: The reason given for deferring the planner change misquotes the scope
findings.evidence: The reading's out-of-scope list names 'the verifier and shared contract prompts' and its assumptions say 'the shared contract and reader prompts are untouched'. The planner frame crates/athena-context/prompts/planner.md is not named there. It is outside scope because it is not a listed deliverable, not because the shared prompts are frozen. Fix: In D189 and the changelog entry, say the planner frame is deferred because it is not among the reading's deliverables. Keep the proposed one-sentence follow-up.
findings.location: Decision 6 / Rejected 'Edit the planner frame in this change'

summary: The plan follows the accepted reading. It adds one pinned paragraph to the change producer prompt and gives it a unit test that fails on the base tree. It also makes the one-number budget edit to docs/system-facts.md, which the budget test forces, and adds a CHANGELOG.md entry and D189. No refusal rule is added. I checked the plan's claims against the code. Producer.md is a single paragraph that ends with the report step. Lib.rs loads it with include_str! at line 21 and has a tests module at line 118. Budgets.rs compares the facts-file line against the computed maximum over capabilities (lines 59 and 109-114), and the headroom rows are computed, not stored. The Bash policy denies shell loops (policy.rs:6-10, athena.toml:84). None of the six criteria matches change_limit (briefs.rs:186-276), so docs/system-facts.md is not sent back. The byte estimate holds: 3127-3129 bytes plus 421 gives 1183-1184 tokens. One design gap remains. The reading's guidance said the producer must report the reproduction command and counts, and a soak run after the fix. The proposed paragraph says only to count failures and never says to report them. The 9daz failure was exactly an unrecorded loop, so that gap stays open. The remaining findings are minor or nits.
